SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK SOF-VD-07: SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition — ViewDefinition.select.repeat. Test these items: repeat 0..* FHIRPath expressions for recursive traversal, view runner recursively follows each path to any depth, multiple repeat paths are combined using union semantics, duplicates and ordering behavior for recursive results, cycle/depth guard behavior under malformed or cyclic structures, columns are evaluated against each repeated node context. For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition.select.repeat: repeat is 0..* string and takes an array of FHIRPath expressions; runner evaluates each expression recursively and unions results from all levels/paths.
issues.evidence: Fresh native and forced-fallback probe with repeat=["item.where(text.exists())"] over QuestionnaireResponse items returned [] on both paths. Expected rows for repeated nodes whose text exists because repeat paths are FHIRPath expressions, not simple dotted property keys.
issues.root_cause: repeat handling treated repeat entries as simple dotted paths and parser validation allowed scalar convenience shape, diverging from the SQL-on-FHIR repeat logical model.
issues.resolution: select.repeat now evaluates entries as FHIRPath expressions in Python fallback and native C++ fhirpath_repeat, collecting object results recursively.
